record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Does the set of ergodic billiard tables have positive measure?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 32 (A. Katok). Does the set of ergodic billiard tables have positive mea-sure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider planar polygonal billiards: given a simple polygon $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, the billiard flow on $P$ is the geodesic flow of a point particle moving in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. For an integer $n\geq 3$, let $T(n)$ denote the space of simple $n$-gons (parametrized, for example, by the $2n$ coordinates of their vertices, modulo rigid motions and scaling), equipped with a natural finite Lebesgue-type probability measure $\lambda$. Let $E(n)\subset T(n)$ be the subset consisting of those $n$-gons whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure on the unit tangent bundle.

It is known that $E(n)$ is a residual (dense $G_\delta$) subset of $T(n)$. The question is:

Does $E(n)$ have positive measure, i.e. is $\lambda(E(n))>0$?
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on billiard dynamics list Katok's question—whether the set of ergodic polygonal billiards has positive measure in the parameter space of polygons—as a well-known open problem. While generic (residual) ergodicity has been established for polygonal billiards, no measure-theoretic version has been proved or disproved, and the question remains open as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Billiard dynamics: An updated survey with the emphasis on open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem: Is λ(E(n)) > 0? The set E(n) of ergodic n-gons is residual in T(n); whether it has positive measure (Katok's question) is open.
status_evidence.claim: Katok's question on positive measure of ergodic polygons is listed as an open problem in a recent billiards survey.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical billiards - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Generic polygons have ergodic billiard flow, but measure-theoretic statements are not known.
status_evidence.claim: Only generic (topological) ergodicity is known; measure-theoretic version remains open.
